newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The government of the Indian state of Tripura has assured Bangaldesh of help in repatriation of tribal Chakma refugees.

Bangladesh-Iran Joint Economic Commission will meet in Dhaka shortly to explore further areas of "sustainable cooperation" between the two countries, said Tehran's Deputy Foreign Minister Alauddin Brujerdi.
The Bangladesh single country trade fair kicked off in Nepalese capital of Kathmandu where the country's niche products ranging from leather goods, chinaware to traditional sarees and fabrics.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Friday asked the tax officials to achieve the collection targets.
India will extend credit facility of rupees 30 crore to Bangladesh.
Seven passengers were killed and 51 others injured when a nigh coach fell into a roadside ditch in northern district of Pabna on Thursday.

Bangladesh has been able to reverse its negative image of "floods, cyclone and famine" to emerge as a land of opportunities for business and investment, Paul Taylor, the leader of a visiting British trade mission said.
North Bengal Paper Mills, a state-run enterprises, is on the verge of closure due to inadequate supply of sweet water for production. REUTER
